Grain's MCP (Model Context Protocol) server gives AI assistants direct access to your meetings, transcripts, AI notes, and workspace data. Ask questions, generate reports, create clips, and organize recordings, all from your AI chat interface.

For technical setup and the full tool reference, see the Grain MCP developer docs.

# Set up with Claude

Step 1: Add the Claude Connector integration

  1. In Claude, go to ’Customize’ → ‘Connectors’

  2. Click '+' to search for connectors

  3. Search for ‘Grain’

  4. Select & connect Grain

  5. You’ll be redirected to Grain to approve the connection

# Official Grain MCP Server: Quick Start Guide

The Grain MCP (Model Context Protocol) connects Claude.ai (and other AI chat clients) directly to your meeting data in Grain, enabling powerful AI-powered individual workflows as well as customer and team analytics/reporting directly within Claude.ai. While we are working on support for ChatGPT (email mike (at) grain (dot) com if you want to be on the ChatGPT early access list), we encourage users who plan to prioritize MCP in their workflow to use Claude as it's support for MCP is currently meaningfully more mature and robust.

# Authentication

Grain supports three authentication methods depending on your use case.

Personal Access Token (PAT): grants access on behalf of a single user. The token has the same permissions as the user who generated it. Best for personal automations or testing. Available on every plan, including Free. Click here to generate a PAT.

Workspace Access Token (WAT): grants access to all data in the workspace, regardless of which user owns it. Use this for server-side integrations where you need workspace-wide access. Requires admin access to generate and is available on Business and Enterprise plans. Click here to generate a WAT.

OAuth2: the standard flow for building integrations to be used by any Grain user. Users authorize your application directly, and your app receives a token scoped to that user's data. Required if you are building an integration to distribute to others.

# Rate limits

The API allows 300 requests per minute per token. Requests beyond this limit return a `429 Too Many Requests` response.

# Authentication

## Authenticating Calls

To authenticate API calls, the client must add the following header:

Copy
    
    `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN`

where `TOKEN` is obtained by one of the methods below.

## Token Types

There are three types of tokens which can have one of two access scopes.

Type  | Scope  | 
--- | --- | ---
Personal Access Token (`PAT`)  | `personal`  | Generated manually from the integrations page.
Doesn't expire, and can be revoked at any time.
Workspace Access Token (`WAT`)  | `workspace`  | Generated manually from the integrations page.
Doesn't expire, and can be revoked at any time.
OAuth Token  | `personal`,
`workspace`  | Issued through the OAuth2 Flow.
Expires, must be refreshed.

Scope  | 
--- | ---
`personal`  | Provides the same access level as the user who authorized the token.
`workspace`  | Provides FULL DATA ACCESS of the workspace.
Can be generated by workspace admins only.

> NOTE: The `workspace` scope is not available on all plans.

pages.text:
Authentication â Grain Developers Authentication Authenticating Calls To authenticate API calls, the client must add the following header: Copy Authorization : Bearer TOKEN where TOKEN is obtained by one of the methods below. Token Types There are three types of tokens which can have one of two access scopes. Type Scope Personal Access Token ( PAT ) personal Generated manually from the integrations page . Doesn't expire, and can be revoked at any time. Workspace Access Token ( WAT ) workspace Generated manually from the integrations page . Doesn't expire, and can be revoked at any time. OAuth Token personal , workspace Issued through the OAuth2 Flow . Expires, must be refreshed. Scope personal Provides the same access level as the user who authorized the token. workspace Provides FULL DATA ACCESS of the workspace. Can be generated by workspace admins only. NOTE: The workspace scope is not available on all plans. Check https://grain.com/pricing to see if your plan includes Workspace API. Tokens with the personal scope, including Personal Access Tokens, also authenticate the Grain MCP server at https://api.grain.com/_/mcp .
Tokens with the workspace scope are not accepted by the MCP server. OAuth2 Flow This authentication method is for developers building integrations with Grain to be used by any Grain users. The API supports a standard OAuth2 Authorization Code flow, including the PKCE extension for client-side only authentication. At least one redirect URI is required to register a new client. For browser-based client applications, a list of CORS origins can also be added. Authorization Code Step 1 Obtain the client_id and client_secret (only for server-side applications) credentials. Step 2 Open the url https://grain.com/_/public-api/oauth2/authorize with the following query params. Param client_id Obtained separately in Step 1 redirect_uri Must exactly match a registered redirect URI. On localhost , 127.0.0.1 and [::1] , any port matches response_type Must be code state Optional. Grain returns it unchanged in Step 4 . PKCE already protects the flow, so state is only needed if your client relies on it code_challenge A random string, hashed with SHA256 and base64 URL encoded code_challenge_method Must be S256 scopes personal or workspace . Defaults to personal Step 3 If the user is not already signed in to Grain, they will be prompted to sign in.
After being authenticated, the user will be prompted to confirm the OAuth2 connection. Step 4 The user will be redirected to redirect_uri from Step 2 with the code query param, and state if you sent one. Step 5 Make a POST request to generate the token.
See OAuth2 Generate Token Diagram sequenceDiagram
  participant you as You
  actor user as User
  participant grain as Grain
  
  Note right of you: Step 1
  you-->>grain: Request Client ID & Secret (manually)
  grain-->>you: Client ID & Secret

  Note right of you: Step 2
  user->>you: Requests OAuth
  you->>user: Open or Redirects to oauth2/authorize
  user->>grain: oauth2/authorize
  
  Note left of grain: Step 3
  grain->>user: Requests login
  user->>grain: Login
  
  grain->>user: Requests Confirm OAuth
  user->>grain: Confirms

	Note left of grain: Step 4  
  grain->>user: Redirects to redirect_uri w/code
  user->>you: redirect_uri w/code
  
  Note right of you: Step 5
  you->>grain: POST oauth2/token w/code
  grain->>you: access_token & refresh_token
  
  Note right of you: Refresh
  you->>grain: POST oauth2/token w/refresh_token
  grain->>you: access_token & refresh_token Client ID Metadata Document Public clients, such as MCP clients and native apps, can skip Step 1 by using an HTTPS URL as their client_id .
That URL must serve a JSON Client ID Metadata Document describing the client. Copy { "client_id" : "https://app.example.com/oauth/client.json" , "client_name" : "Example App" , "redirect_uris" : [ "https://app.example.com/oauth/callback" ] , "grant_types" : [ "authorization_code" , "refresh_token" ] , "response_types" : [ "code" ] , "token_endpoint_auth_method" : "none" } Field client_id Required. Must exactly match the URL the document is served from redirect_uris Required. The redirect_uri in Step 2 must exactly match one of these client_name Shown to the user when they confirm the connection. Defaults to the URL's host grant_types Must include authorization_code . Add refresh_token to receive refresh tokens response_types Must be code if present token_endpoint_auth_method Must be none if present. Client secrets are not supported Grain applies these rules to documents and their clients: The URL must use https and serve the document directly, with no redirects, in at most 5 KB. Grain caches the document for the max-age in its Cache-Control header, between 5 minutes and 24 hours, and revalidates it with its ETag . PKCE is required, so send code_challenge in Step 2 and code_verifier when generating the token. http redirect URIs are only allowed on localhost , 127.0.0.1 and [::1] , where any port matches. The workspace scope is only available to clients verified by Grain. Refresh Token After the access_token has expired, you may generate a new one. See OAuth2 Refresh Token On this page Authenticating Calls Token Types OAuth2 Flow Authorization Code Client ID Metadata Document Refresh Token

pages.title: Grain API | Grain (https://support.grain.com/en/articles/15507288-grain-api)
pages.text: Grain API | Grain Skip to main content Grain API Connect Grain to your own tools and workflows with the Grain public API. Updated over a month ago Table of contents The Grain API lets developers read meeting data, manage recordings, and receive real-time events from Grain programmatically. Use it to build custom integrations, sync data to internal systems, or automate workflows that go beyond what Grain's built-in integrations support. For the full technical reference, see developers.grain.com . What you can do with the API Read meeting data : retrieve recordings, transcripts, AI notes and action items, participants, tags, teams, and meeting types from your workspace. Manage recordings : upload external recordings to Grain, update recording metadata, add or remove tags, and control sharing at the user or team level. Download recordings : export video files and transcripts in multiple formats (JSON, plain text, VTT, SRT) for archiving or processing. Receive real-time events : register webhooks to receive a payload whenever a new recording is processed in your workspace, so downstream systems stay in sync without polling. Authentication Grain supports three authentication methods depending on your use case. Personal Access Token (PAT) : grants access on behalf of a single user. The token has the same permissions as the user who generated it. Best for personal automations or testing. Available on every plan, including Free. Click here to generate a PAT. Workspace Access Token (WAT) : grants access to all data in the workspace, regardless of which user owns it. Use this for server-side integrations where you need workspace-wide access. Requires admin access to generate and is available on Business and Enterprise plans. Click here to generate a WAT. OAuth2 : the standard flow for building integrations to be used by any Grain user. Users authorize your application directly, and your app receives a token scoped to that user's data. Required if you are building an integration to distribute to others. Rate limits The API allows 300 requests per minute per token. Requests beyond this limit return a 429 Too Many Requests response. Each response includes rate limit headers so you can track remaining capacity. Webhooks Webhooks let Grain push data to your system when events occur, rather than requiring you to poll for changes. Register a webhook URL in your integration and Grain will send a payload to that URL whenever a registered event occurs, for example, a new recording is processed, a recording's settings change, or a clip is created. See the developer docs for the full list of supported event types. API version The current API version is 2025-10-31 . All requests must include a Public-Api-Version header with this value. Grain uses versioning to introduce and deprecate fields without breaking existing integrations. The v1 (beta) API was sunset in September 2026. Use v2 for all integrations. See the developer docs for migration details. FAQ Do I need a specific Grain plan to use the API? Not for personal API access, which is available on every plan, including Free. Workspace API access is available on Business and Enterprise plans and requires admin access to generate. Can I access recordings I did not attend? With a Personal Access Token, you can only access recordings within your own permission level. With a Workspace Access Token, you can access all recordings in the workspace. Can I upload recordings from other platforms into Grain? Yes. The API supports uploading external recordings, which Grain will then transcribe and process as if they were captured natively. Where do I generate my API token? Personal API tokens are generated in Account settings → Integrations → Personal API . They are available on every plan. Workspace API tokens are generated in Workspace settings → Integrations → API . Only workspace admins on Business and Enterprise plans can generate API tokens for the workspace. Is there a sandbox environment for testing? No sandbox is available at this time. Test against your live workspace using a Personal Access Token scoped to your own account to limit exposure. Next up: AI Transcript Actions Did this answer your question? Disappointed Reaction 😞 Neutral Reaction 😐 Smiley Reaction 😃 Table of contents

Updated over a week ago Table of contents Grain's MCP (Model Context Protocol) server gives AI assistants direct access to your meetings, transcripts, AI notes, and workspace data. Ask questions, generate reports, create clips, and organize recordings, all from your AI chat interface. For technical setup and the full tool reference, see the Grain MCP developer docs . Set up with Claude Step 1: Add the Claude Connector integration In Claude, go to ’Customize’ → ‘Connectors’ Click '+' to search for connectors Search for ‘Grain’ Select & connect Grain You’ll be redirected to Grain to approve the connection Step 2: Verify From a new Claude chat, send this test prompt: Tell me about my most recent Grain meeting If the MCP doesn’t work as expected, click '+' and confirm 'Grain' appears under 'Connectors' before trying again. Set up with ChatGPT Step 1: Add the ChatGPT App integration Go to 'Apps' and search for 'Grain' Select 'Grain' and click 'Connect' Sign in and approve ChatGPT access to your Grain account data Step 2: Verify From a new ChatGPT chat, send the following test prompt: Tell me about my most recent Grain meeting If the MCP doesn’t work properly, click '+' and select Grain as a source before trying again. Set up with Cursor Click the link below to install with a single command: Set up Grain in Cursor → What the Grain MCP can do All plans Search meetings by company, person, date range, or topic Get transcripts and AI-generated notes for any meeting Retrieve action items from a meeting Access your private notes on a recording Create clips from any meeting Tag meetings to organize your workspace Create and manage playlists and stories Business & Enterprise plans Get AI-generated sales coaching insights and scorecards Access deal intelligence via HubSpot integration Get Grain's Company Memory for context about the companies you work with across all your meetings Share or unshare meetings with your teams or the whole workspace For the full tool list and parameters, see Available MCP Tools . Example prompts Meeting research "Show me all action items I'm responsible for from the past 7 days." "Who from Acme Corp have we met with and what topics did we cover?" "What objections came up in external sales calls this week?" Content creation "Clip the section where the client talks about their timeline." "Tag all meetings from last week with external participants as #client-calls." "Create a playlist called 'Onboarding Best Practices' and add my last five training calls." Pre-built reports Grain provides structured report prompts accessible in Claude via ’+’ → ‘Connectors’ → ‘Add from Grain’. These chain multiple steps into full reports. Report Best for Plan required Voice of Customer Insights Product priorities, market trends Any plan Recently Active Accounts Health Portfolio triage, churn risk Any plan Customer Health by Account Renewal planning, expansion Any plan SPICED Opportunity Matrix (Account) Retention strategy, QBR prep Any plan Deal Pipeline Intelligence Portfolio overview, forecasting Business or Enterprise Health Report by Deal Deal strategy, next steps Business or Enterprise SPICED Opportunity Matrix (Deal) Deal qualification Business or Enterprise MEDDICC Diagnosis Enterprise deal qualification Business or Enterprise Sales Team Performance & Coaching Training priorities, performance trends Business or Enterprise FAQ Is my data safe? Grain's MCP server uses OAuth and HTTPS. Developers can also connect with a personal access token; see the developer docs . Your data stays in your Grain account and is processed temporarily by AI to answer your questions. View your connected AI client's privacy policy for more information about data handling. What data can the MCP access? Only data you already have access to in Grain — meetings you attended, contacts, AI notes, transcripts, and deal info (with HubSpot connected). It cannot access meetings you weren't part of. Can I control which capabilities my AI client uses? Yes. In Claude’s ‘Connectors’ menu you can toggle individual Grain tools on or off. ChatGPT offers a similar feature, allowing you to specify when ChatGPT should ask for permission to use an MCP tool. Next up: API Did this answer your question? pages.title: Frequently Asked Questions — Grain Developers (https://developers.grain.com/mcp/faq.html)
pages.text: Frequently Asked Questions â Grain Developers Frequently Asked Questions Q: What applications and platforms support MCP integrations? A: The Model Context Protocol is rapidly gaining adoption where each client supports different MCP features (tools, prompts, resources) depending on their use cases. For the semi-complete list of Clients with feature compatibility details, visit the official MCP clients directory . Q: What Claude plan do I need to use MCP integrations? A: MCP integrations, including the Grain MCP server, are only available on paid Claude plans (Pro, Team, and Enterprise). Free Claude accounts do not support MCP integrations or the ability to connect external tools and data sources. You'll need to upgrade to a paid plan to access the Grain integration and other MCP servers. Q: Are all Grain MCP tools available on every Grain plan? A: Most Grain MCP tools work on all Grain plans (Free, Starter, Business, Enterprise), including meeting search, transcripts, notes, and contact management. However, tools for Deals ( list_open_deals , list_all_deals , fetch_deal ) and Sales Coaching/Scorecards ( list_coaching_feedback , fetch_meeting_coaching_feedback ) are restricted to Business and Enterprise plan users only. Free and Starter plan users will receive an error if they attempt to use these premium tools. Q: Is it safe to use MCP servers like Grain's? A: MCP security relies on a trust model, and Grain's MCP server is officially supported by us and aligns with our existing security practices, follows the MCP specification exactly, and uses industry-standard OAuth authentication and HTTPS. All tool usage requires explicit user approval in Claude, and each tool request is scoped to specific data needed for that operation. While no system is 100% secure, Grain's established security practices and transparent approach to data handling make it a safer MCP implementation. Q: How does the Model Context Protocol (MCP) work and what are the privacy implications? A: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that creates a secure bridge between Claude and external services like Grain, where your data stays in your Grain account and is only processed temporarily by Claude to answer questions. As stated by Anthropic , data accessed through MCP integrations is not used to train Claude's models. Q: What data does Grain's MCP server have access to? A: Grain's MCP server only accesses data you already have permission to view in your Grain workspace, including meetings you attended, companies and contacts from those meetings, deal information (with HubSpot integration), and AI-generated notes and transcripts. It has no access to private meetings you weren't invited to or other workspaces you don't belong to. The integration uses OAuth authentication and maintains the same security boundaries as your normal Grain usage. Q: How does Claude verify and approve MCP tool usage? A: Claude requires explicit user approval before using any Grain tool, showing you a dialog with clear descriptions of what each tool will do and offering "use once" or "use for entire session" options. Each tool requires separate approval when first used, and you maintain control over which tools Claude can access in your current session. You can revoke access by starting a new chat session, ensuring that no tools run without your explicit permission. Q: Can I control what data the Grain MCP server shares with Claude? A: Data access is controlled through your existing Grain account permissions, and you can enable/disable specific tools in Claude's integration settings, but you cannot currently exclude specific meetings or companies from MCP access. The integration accesses all data you have permission to see in your Grain workspace and follows your existing permissions rather than providing additional filtering options. Review your Grain workspace permissions before connecting and use targeted prompts to limit the scope of data Claude requests. Q: What is the helpful_usage_information parameter I see in the client's tool responses? A: You may notice the helpful_usage_information parameter appearing in chat interface when the Grain MCP server responds to tool requests. This optional parameter helps Grain's team understand tool usage patterns to improve functionality, and this data is never used as AI training data. Currently there's no opt-out option, but one will be available in the coming months - if you're uncomfortable with this data collection, consider waiting until then.
